components.note: 田 (field) — 町 originally named the raised path or ridge running between fields.
丁 (dīng) shares 町's final sound -ing but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 农民沿着田边的町走到地里。
example.pinyin: Nóngmín yánzhe tiánbiān de tīng zǒu dào dì lǐ.
example.english: The farmer walked along the raised path between the fields to get to the plot.
example.fact: Japan later borrowed this same character to name 町 (chō/machi), an administrative unit for towns and city blocks — a meaning descended from its original sense of a raised path dividing farm fields.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 芥 names a plant in the mustard family.
介 (jiè) gives an exact match for 芥's reading.

example.hanzi: 吃日本料理时常配芥末。
example.pinyin: Chī Rìběn liàolǐ shí cháng pèi jièmò.
example.english: People often pair Japanese cuisine with mustard.
example.fact: The idiom 芥蒂 (jièdì) uses this character metaphorically: like a mustard seed lodged in the throat, it describes a small, lingering grudge or resentment between people.

components.note: 疒 (sickness, ailment) — 瘠 describes a body wasted thin by illness or poor nourishment.
脊 (jí) gives an exact match for 瘠's reading — 脊 itself means 'spine, backbone,' echoing a body so thin its bones show.

example.hanzi: 这片土地十分贫瘠,农作物长不好。
example.pinyin: Zhè piàn tǔdì shífēn pínjí, nóngzuòwù zhǎng bù hǎo.
example.english: This land is very barren, and crops don't grow well here.
example.fact: 瘠 pairs the sickness radical 疒 with 脊 ('spine'), reflecting an original image of a body so emaciated its backbone shows — the same character also describes soil too thin and poor to nourish good crops, as in 贫瘠 (pínjí, 'barren').

components.note: 门 (gate, door) — 阂 relates to something that blocks or separates, like a barred gate.
亥 (hài) shares 阂's initial sound but not the full syllable — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 长期不联系让他们之间产生了隔阂。
example.pinyin: Chángqī bù liánxì ràng tāmen zhījiān chǎnshēng le géhé.
example.english: Not being in touch for a long time created a rift between them.
example.fact: 隔阂 (géhé), literally 'a separating gate,' describes an emotional or communicative barrier between people — the character's 门 (gate) radical is still visible in this figurative sense of being shut off from one another.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 挎 describes carrying something using the arm or hand.
夸 (kuā) is close to 挎's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 她挎着一个篮子去市场。
example.pinyin: Tā kuà zhe yí gè lánzi qù shìchǎng.
example.english: She carried a basket on her arm to the market.
example.fact: 挎 specifically describes carrying something hooked over an arm, shoulder, or hip — distinct from 提 (carrying by a handle) or 背 (carrying on the back), reflecting how precise Mandarin verbs for 'carrying' are about body position.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 橇 names a wooden sled or sledge used for traveling over snow or ice.
毳 (cuì) no longer resembles 橇's modern reading qiāo — the sound has drifted far apart over time.

example.hanzi: 冬天,孩子们喜欢坐雪橇滑下山坡。
example.pinyin: Dōngtiān, háizimen xǐhuan zuò xuěqiāo huá xià shānpō.
example.english: In winter, children love sliding down the hillside on sleds.
example.fact: 雪橇 is also the official Chinese term for luge and other sliding sports at the Winter Olympics, where competitors race down ice-covered tracks at high speed.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 荟 originally described plants growing thick and luxuriant.
会 (huì) gives an exact match for 荟's reading.

example.hanzi: 这次展览荟萃了世界各地的艺术精品。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì zhǎnlǎn huìcuì le shìjiè gèdì de yìshù jīngpǐn.
example.english: This exhibition brought together fine artworks from all over the world.
example.fact: 荟萃 (huìcuì) keeps the image of plants growing thick together, and the phrase 人才荟萃 (réncái huìcuì) borrows it to describe a place where many talented people have gathered.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 啜 describes drinking, sipping, or the sound made while sobbing.
叕 (zhuó) no longer resembles 啜's modern reading chuò — the sound has drifted apart over time, though it's traditionally treated as the phonetic component.

example.hanzi: 她一边啜泣,一边讲述事情的经过。
example.pinyin: Tā yìbiān chuòqì, yìbiān jiǎngshù shìqing de jīngguò.
example.english: She sobbed as she recounted what had happened.
example.fact: 啜 has more than one historical reading — Chinese dictionaries also record it as a rare surname read chuài — but in its everyday meanings of 'to sip' or 'to sob' (as in 啜泣, chuòqì), the standard modern reading is chuò.

components.note: 土 (earth, soil) — 垛 originally described a mound or pile of earth.
朵 (duǒ) gives an exact match for 垛's reading.

example.hanzi: 秋收后,农民把麦秸堆成垛。
example.pinyin: Qiūshōu hòu, nóngmín bǎ màijiē duī chéng duǒ.
example.english: After the autumn harvest, farmers pile the wheat straw into stacks.
example.fact: 箭垛 (jiàn duǒ) originally referred to earthen mounds on ancient city walls used as archery targets or defensive parapets — the same character now also names an ordinary haystack, both senses sharing the image of material piled up high.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 淇 names a river; it appears in the name of the Qi River (淇河) in Henan.
其 (qí) gives an exact match for 淇's reading.

example.hanzi: 淇河发源于河南省,在《诗经》中多次被提及。
example.pinyin: Qíhé fāyuán yú Hénán Shěng, zài Shījīng zhōng duō cì bèi tíjí.
example.english: The Qi River originates in Henan Province and is mentioned many times in the Book of Songs.
example.fact: The Qi River (淇河) is celebrated in the Book of Songs (诗经), China's oldest collection of poetry, in verses describing its banks in the ancient state of Wey.

components.note: 王 (here the 玉 radical, 'jade') — 瓒 names a ceremonial cup carved from or trimmed with jade.
赞 (zàn) gives an exact match for 瓒's reading.

example.hanzi: 古代祭祀时,天子常用玉瓒盛酒。
example.pinyin: Gǔdài jìsì shí, tiānzǐ chángyòng yùzàn chéng jiǔ.
example.english: During ancient sacrificial rites, the emperor often used a jade ceremonial cup to hold wine.
example.fact: 圭瓒 (guīzàn), a jade-handled ceremonial ladle, was used to pour wine in ancestral sacrifices during the Zhou dynasty and is described in classical ritual texts such as the Book of Rites.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 篓 names a basket woven from bamboo strips.
娄 (lóu) is close to 篓's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 山区的农民常用背篓运送货物。
example.pinyin: Shānqū de nóngmín chángyòng bēilǒu yùnsòng huòwù.
example.english: Farmers in mountain regions often use bamboo backpack-baskets to transport goods.
example.fact: 背篓 (bēilǒu), a woven bamboo basket carried on the back with a strap over the shoulders, remains a common way to transport goods on foot in China's mountainous southwest, where narrow paths make wheeled carts impractical.

components.note: 虫 (insect, worm) — 虱 names a tiny parasitic insect, the louse.
乙 (yǐ) shares 虱's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 头发太久不洗容易长虱子。
example.pinyin: Tóufa tài jiǔ bù xǐ róngyì zhǎng shīzi.
example.english: If hair isn't washed for a long time, lice can easily grow in it.
example.fact: Lice have coevolved with humans for so long that geneticists have compared the DNA of head lice and body lice to estimate when humans first began wearing clothing — roughly 170,000 years ago.

meanings: (literary) to ascend; to climb; to mount

components.note: 足 (foot) — 跻 describes rising or climbing, an action rooted in stepping upward.
齐 (qí) shares 跻's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 这家公司跻身世界500强。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī jīshēn shìjiè wǔbǎi qiáng.
example.english: This company has risen into the ranks of the Fortune Global 500.
example.fact: 跻身 literally means to 'ascend into' a group, and 世界500强 (Fortune Global 500) is the standard Chinese name for the annual ranking of the world's largest companies by revenue.

components.note: 龙 (dragon) is 龛's official radical, though the connection is more graphic than semantic — Buddhist and Daoist shrine niches are often carved with dragon motifs, but the character's meaning doesn't literally involve dragons.
合 (hé) no longer resembles 龛's modern reading kān — the sound has drifted apart over time, though it's traditionally treated as the phonetic component.

example.hanzi: 奶奶家的墙上有一个供奉观音的佛龛。
example.pinyin: Nǎinai jiā de qiáng shàng yǒu yí gè gòngfèng Guānyīn de fókān.
example.english: There's a Buddhist shrine niche on the wall of grandma's house enshrining Guanyin.
example.fact: 佛龛 (fókān), a small recessed niche or cabinet for enshrining a Buddha or deity statue, remains a common household fixture in traditional Chinese and Southeast Asian homes, often placed high on a wall for daily incense offerings.

meanings: used in 蹣跚|蹒跚[pan2 shan1]

components.note: 足 (foot) — 蹒 relates to the motion of walking, specifically an unsteady, tottering gait.
㒼 (mán) shares 蹒's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 老人蹒跚地走在雪地里。
example.pinyin: Lǎorén pánshān de zǒu zài xuě dì lǐ.
example.english: The old man walked unsteadily through the snow.
example.fact: 蹒跚 (pánshān) exists almost only as this fixed two-character word describing a slow, tottering gait — often used for the elderly or infirm — and is one of many Chinese descriptive binomes built from characters that rarely appear alone.

components.note: 髟 (long, flowing hair) — 髯 names facial hair, specifically a beard or whiskers.
冉 (rǎn) is close to 髯's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 小说中,关羽以髯长而闻名,被称为美髯公。
example.pinyin: Xiǎoshuō zhōng, Guān Yǔ yǐ rán cháng ér wénmíng, bèi chēng wéi Měirángōng.
example.english: In the novel, Guan Yu is famous for his long beard and is called 'the Lord of the Beautiful Beard.'
example.fact: In the classic novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms, the general Guan Yu is nicknamed 美髯公 (Měirángōng, 'Lord of the Beautiful Beard') for his long beard — a nickname still referenced in Chinese opera and art depicting him.

components.note: 目 (eye) — 瞠 describes a fixed, wide-eyed stare, often from shock.
堂 (táng) no longer resembles 瞠's modern reading chēng — the sound has drifted apart over time, though it's traditionally treated as the phonetic component.

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息,大家都瞠目结舌。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, dàjiā dōu chēngmù jiéshé.
example.english: Hearing this news, everyone was left stunned and speechless.
example.fact: 瞠目结舌 (chēngmù jiéshé) is a four-character idiom combining 'staring eyes' (瞠目) with 'a knotted tongue' (结舌) to describe someone so shocked that they can neither look away nor speak.

components.note: 疒 (sickness, ailment) — 痫 names a neurological illness, epilepsy.
闲 (xián) gives an exact match for 痫's reading.

example.hanzi: 癫痫患者需要按时服药以控制病情。
example.pinyin: Diānxián huànzhě xūyào ànshí fúyào yǐ kòngzhì bìngqíng.
example.english: Epilepsy patients need to take medication on schedule to control their condition.
example.fact: 癫痫 (diānxián) is the standard modern Chinese medical term for epilepsy; traditional Chinese medicine once called it 羊痫风 ('goat-epilepsy wind'), based on the jerking convulsions observed during seizures resembling a goat's movements.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 掂 describes judging weight by holding something in the hand.
店 (diàn) is close to 掂's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 买水果前,他喜欢用手掂一掂,估计重量。
example.pinyin: Mǎi shuǐguǒ qián, tā xǐhuan yòng shǒu diān yi diān, gūjì zhòngliàng.
example.english: Before buying fruit, he likes to heft it in his hand to estimate its weight.
example.fact: 掂量 (diānliáng) extends from its literal sense of physically weighing something in the hand to a common figurative meaning: mentally weighing up a decision before acting.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 潼 appears in river and place names, including Tongguan Pass (潼关), named for the waters nearby.
童 (tóng) gives an exact match for 潼's reading.

example.hanzi: 潼关自古就是兵家必争之地。
example.pinyin: Tóngguān zìgǔ jiùshì bīngjiā bìzhēng zhī dì.
example.english: Tongguan Pass has been a strategically contested site since ancient times.
example.fact: 潼关 (Tongguan Pass), where the Yellow, Wei, and Luo rivers meet near the borders of Shaanxi, Shanxi, and Henan, has been one of China's most fought-over strategic passes for over two thousand years.

components.note: 酉 (originally 'wine, alcohol,' extended to chemical terms) — 酰 is a modern character coined for chemistry, naming the acyl functional group.
先 (xiān) gives an exact match for 酰's reading.

example.hanzi: 阿司匹林的化学名称中含有乙酰基。
example.pinyin: Āsīpǐlín de huàxué míngchēng zhōng hányǒu yǐxiānjī.
example.english: Aspirin's chemical name contains an acetyl group.
example.fact: Aspirin's formal chemical name is acetylsalicylic acid (乙酰水杨酸) — the 酰 (xiān, 'acyl') here marks the acetyl group that gives the drug its name and much of its effect.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 镁 names the metallic element magnesium.
美 (měi) gives an exact match for 镁's reading.

example.hanzi: 镁是人体骨骼和肌肉正常运作所需的矿物质。
example.pinyin: Měi shì réntǐ gǔgé hé jīròu zhèngcháng yùnzuò suǒ xū de kuàngwùzhì.
example.english: Magnesium is a mineral the body needs for normal bone and muscle function.
example.fact: Magnesium metal burns with an intensely bright white light, which is why it was used in early photography flash powder and is still used today in flares, fireworks, and sparklers.

components.note: 火 (fire) — 灸 names the therapy of burning dried herbs to apply heat to the body.
久 (jiǔ) gives an exact match for 灸's reading.

example.hanzi: 中医常用针灸来治疗慢性疼痛。
example.pinyin: Zhōngyī chángyòng zhēnjiǔ lái zhìliáo mànxìng téngtòng.
example.english: Traditional Chinese medicine often uses acupuncture and moxibustion to treat chronic pain.
example.fact: 针灸 ('acupuncture and moxibustion') combines two distinct therapies: 针 (needling) and 灸 (burning dried mugwort on or near the skin), whose warmth is believed in TCM theory to stimulate circulation along the body's meridians.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, body) — 腆 relates to a part of the body, specifically a protruding belly.
典 (diǎn) shares 腆's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 他腆着肚子走了进来。
example.pinyin: Tā tiǎn zhe dùzi zǒu le jìnlái.
example.english: He walked in with his belly stuck out.
example.fact: 腆 appears in the common colloquial phrase 腆着肚子 (tiǎn zhe dùzi), describing someone puffing out their belly, often used to humorously describe a self-important or well-fed strut.

etymologyHint: Distant 攸 bamboo ⺮; 小 provides the pronunciation

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 筱 names a slender, dwarf variety of bamboo traditionally used for arrows and fishing rods.

example.hanzi: 筱是一种细小的竹子,古人常用来做箭杆。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo shì yì zhǒng xìxiǎo de zhúzi, gǔrén cháng yòng lái zuò jiàn gǎn.
example.english: Xiao is a kind of thin, slender bamboo that ancient people often used to make arrow shafts.
example.fact: 筱 is now mostly seen not in botanical contexts but as a delicate-sounding character chosen for given names (such as 筱雨 or 筱婷), valued for its refined, nature-evoking sound rather than its original meaning of thin bamboo.

etymologyHint: One who freely shares 享 advice 讠; 享 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 讠 (speech, words) — 谆 describes speech that is earnest, patient, and repeated, as in giving careful advice.
享 (xiǎng) no longer resembles 谆's modern reading zhūn — despite historically being treated as this character's phonetic element, the sound has drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 老师的谆谆教诲让我终生难忘。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī de zhūnzhūn jiàohuì ràng wǒ zhōngshēng nánwàng.
example.english: My teacher's earnest and patient guidance left a lifelong impression on me.
example.fact: 谆谆教诲 (zhūnzhūn jiàohuì) is a common set phrase praising a teacher's or elder's patient, repeated moral guidance — 谆 itself almost never appears outside this reduplicated form.

components.note: 马 (horse) — 骋 describes a horse running freely, at a gallop.
甹 (pīng) no longer resembles 骋's modern reading chěng — the sound has drifted apart over time, though it's traditionally treated as the phonetic component.

example.hanzi: 他年轻时曾驰骋商场,创立了自己的企业。
example.pinyin: Tā niánqīng shí céng chíchěng shāngchǎng, chuànglì le zìjǐ de qǐyè.
example.english: In his youth he once thrived in the business world, founding his own company.
example.fact: 驰骋 (chíchěng) literally means 'to gallop a horse freely' but is very often used figuratively today, as in 驰骋商场 ('to range freely through the business world').

example.hanzi: 壬寅年对应十二生肖中的虎年。
example.pinyin: Rén yín nián duìyìng shí'èr shēngxiào zhōng de hǔ nián.
example.english: A Renyin year corresponds to the Year of the Tiger in the zodiac cycle.
example.fact: 壬 is one of the ten Heavenly Stems (天干) that, combined with the twelve Earthly Branches (地支), form the sexagenary 60-year cycle traditionally used in the Chinese calendar to name years, days, and hours.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 茗 names the tea plant and its leaves.
名 (míng) gives an exact match for 茗's reading.

example.hanzi: 周末,他喜欢约朋友去茶馆品茗。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò, tā xǐhuan yuē péngyou qù cháguǎn pǐnmíng.
example.english: On weekends, he likes to invite friends to a teahouse to savor tea.
example.fact: 茗 is a more literary, elegant word for tea than the everyday 茶, often seen in teahouse and tea-brand names, or in refined phrases like 品茗 ('to savor tea').

meanings: used in 椋鳥|椋鸟[liang2 niao3]

components.note: 木 (tree) — historically linked to a tree the bird favored, though today 椋 survives mainly in the bird's name 椋鸟.
京 (jīng) no longer resembles 椋's modern reading liáng — the sound has drifted apart over time, though it's traditionally treated as the phonetic component.

example.hanzi: 椋鸟经常成群飞过城市上空。
example.pinyin: Liángniǎo jīngcháng chéngqún fēiguò chéngshì shàngkōng.
example.english: Starlings often fly over cities in large flocks.
example.fact: 椋鸟 (starlings) are known for forming enormous, swirling flocks called murmurations at dusk — a striking natural phenomenon studied by scientists for insight into collective animal behavior.

components.note: 虫 (insect, worm) — 蛔 names a parasitic intestinal worm.
回 (huí) gives an exact match for 蛔's reading.

example.hanzi: 小孩子肚子疼,可能是感染了蛔虫。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi dùzi téng, kěnéng shì gǎnrǎn le huíchóng.
example.english: The child's stomachache might be caused by a roundworm infection.
example.fact: 蛔虫 (roundworms) were historically extremely common intestinal parasites in China before modern sanitation, and Chinese schools once routinely administered deworming medicine to students.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 潺 describes the sound of gently flowing water.
孱 (càn) shares 潺's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 溪水潺潺地流过山谷。
example.pinyin: Xīshuǐ chánchán de liúguò shāngǔ.
example.english: The stream flowed gently, babbling through the valley.
example.fact: 潺潺 (chánchán) is an onomatopoeic word imitating the soft babbling sound of a small stream, and appears frequently in classical Chinese poetry describing peaceful natural scenes.

components.note: 户 (door) — 扉 names a door panel or leaf.
非 (fēi) gives an exact match for 扉's reading.

example.hanzi: 这次谈话让他敞开了心扉。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì tánhuà ràng tā chǎngkāi le xīnfēi.
example.english: This conversation made him open up his heart.
example.fact: 心扉 (xīnfēi, literally 'the door of the heart') is a common figurative phrase for someone's innermost feelings — to '敞开心扉' means to open up emotionally to another person.

components.note: 耒 (plow, farming tool) — 耘 describes tending a field, specifically removing weeds.
云 (yún) gives an exact match for 耘's reading.

example.hanzi: 他多年辛勤耕耘,终于取得了成功。
example.pinyin: Tā duōnián xīnqín gēngyún, zhōngyú qǔdé le chénggōng.
example.english: After years of hard work and dedication, he finally achieved success.
example.fact: 耕耘 (gēngyún, literally 'to plow and weed') is widely used figuratively for sustained hard work toward a goal, as in the saying 一分耕耘,一分收获 ('one part toil, one part harvest').

meanings: used in 檳子|槟子[bin1 zi5]
used in 檳榔|槟榔[bing1 lang5]

components.note: 木 (tree) — 槟 names the areca palm and its nut.
宾 (bīn) gives an exact match for 槟's reading.

example.hanzi: 在中国南方和东南亚,有些人喜欢嚼槟榔。
example.pinyin: Zài Zhōngguó nánfāng hé Dōngnányà, yǒuxiē rén xǐhuan jiáo bīnláng.
example.english: In southern China and Southeast Asia, some people like to chew betel nut.
example.fact: 槟榔 (the areca/betel nut) is chewed as a mild stimulant across South and Southeast Asia and parts of southern China, but the World Health Organization classifies it as a carcinogen linked to oral cancer.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — 雹 names a form of precipitation, hail.
包 (bāo) is close to 雹's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 昨天下了一场冰雹,把车窗都砸坏了。
example.pinyin: Zuótiān xià le yì chǎng bīngbáo, bǎ chē chuāng dōu zá huài le.
example.english: Yesterday a hailstorm hit and smashed the car windows.
example.fact: 冰雹 (hail) forms when strong updrafts inside thunderstorms repeatedly carry ice pellets upward through freezing layers of cloud, adding a new layer of ice each time before they finally fall.

meanings: path screened by walls on both sides

components.note: 用 (yòng) is close to 甬's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 宁波有一个别称叫甬城。
example.pinyin: Níngbō yǒu yí gè biéchēng jiào Yǒngchéng.
example.english: Ningbo has an alternate name: Yong City.
example.fact: 甬 is the classical single-character abbreviation for the city of Ningbo (宁波), still seen today at the start of Ningbo's vehicle license plates.

meanings: (literary) to confer a posthumous name or title

components.note: 讠 (speech, words) — 谥 describes the formal act of conferring a title in words after someone's death.
益 (yì) shares 谥's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 皇帝驾崩后,大臣们为他议定谥号。
example.pinyin: Huángdì jiàbēng hòu, dàchénmen wéi tā yìdìng shìhào.
example.english: After the emperor's death, his ministers deliberated and decided on his posthumous title.
example.fact: A 谥号 (posthumous title) was formally conferred on Chinese emperors and officials after death to sum up their reign or character — for instance, Emperor Wu of Han's title 武 ('martial') is where his common name comes from.

meanings: name of a river in Jiangsu
name of a river in Jiangsu Province

components.note: 氵 (water) — 淞 names a river; it appears in Wusong (吴淞), a river and district near Shanghai.
松 (sōng) gives an exact match for 淞's reading.

example.hanzi: 吴淞江是上海地区重要的河流之一。
example.pinyin: Wúsōngjiāng shì Shànghǎi dìqū zhòngyào de héliú zhī yī.
example.english: The Wusong River is one of the important rivers in the Shanghai area.
example.fact: 吴淞 (Wusong), where the Huangpu River meets the Yangtze estuary near Shanghai, was the site of key battles during the Japanese invasions of Shanghai in 1932 and 1937.

components.note: 火 (fire) — 燎 describes burning or setting something ablaze.
尞 (liào) is close to 燎's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 星星之火,可以燎原。
example.pinyin: Xīngxīng zhī huǒ, kěyǐ liáoyuán.
example.english: A single spark can set the whole prairie ablaze.
example.fact: 星星之火,可以燎原 is a famous phrase associated with a 1930 essay by Mao Zedong, using the image of a small flame growing into an unstoppable wildfire as a metaphor for how a small movement could spread nationwide.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 蕙 names a fragrant orchid.
惠 (huì) gives an exact match for 蕙's reading.

example.hanzi: 人们常用蕙质兰心来形容一个女子的高雅气质。
example.pinyin: Rénmen chángyòng huìzhì lánxīn lái xíngróng yí gè nǚzǐ de gāoyǎ qìzhì.
example.english: People often use the phrase 'orchid heart, orchid nature' to describe a woman's refined and elegant character.
example.fact: 蕙质兰心 (huìzhì lánxīn) pairs two orchid-family plants, 蕙 and 兰, as a compliment for a woman's inner refinement — a phrase still common in literary Chinese today.

components.note: 虫 (insect, worm) — used loosely here for a small aquatic creature; 蚪 names the tadpole.
斗 (dòu) is close to 蚪's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 池塘里有很多小蝌蚪在游来游去。
example.pinyin: Chítáng lǐ yǒu hěn duō xiǎo kēdǒu zài yóulái yóuqù.
example.english: There are many little tadpoles swimming around in the pond.
example.fact: 蝌蚪 (tadpoles) are the subject of a beloved Chinese children's story, 小蝌蚪找妈妈 ('Little Tadpoles Looking for Their Mother'), a classic 1960 ink-wash animated film.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — 蜻 names an insect, the dragonfly.
青 (qīng) gives an exact match for 蜻's reading.

example.hanzi: 夏天的池塘边常常能看到蜻蜓飞舞。
example.pinyin: Xiàtiān de chítáng biān chángcháng néng kàndào qīngtíng fēiwǔ.
example.english: In summer, dragonflies can often be seen flitting around the pond.
example.fact: Dragonflies have hunted in essentially their current form for roughly 300 million years, predating dinosaurs, and their compound eyes contain up to 30,000 individual lenses, giving them near 360-degree vision.

components.note: 阝 (here the 邑 radical, 'settlement, place') — 郸 is used only in the place name Handan (邯郸).
单 (dān) gives an exact match for 郸's reading.

example.hanzi: 邯郸是一座有着三千多年历史的古城。
example.pinyin: Hándān shì yí zuò yǒuzhe sānqiān duō nián lìshǐ de gǔchéng.
example.english: Handan is an ancient city with a history of more than three thousand years.
example.fact: 邯郸 was the capital of the state of Zhao during the Warring States period and is the origin of the idiom 邯郸学步 ('learning to walk in Handan'), about a man who imitated the local gait so hard he forgot how to walk at all.

components.note: 车 (cart, vehicle) — 轶 originally described one carriage overtaking or rushing past another.
失 (shī) shares 轶's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 这本书记录了许多名人轶事。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū jìlù le xǔduō míngrén yìshì.
example.english: This book records many anecdotes about famous people.
example.fact: 轶事 (yìshì, anecdotes) refers to minor, little-known stories about a person's life that don't appear in official biographies — from 轶's original meaning of one carriage overtaking another, extended to information that has 'slipped past' the historical record.

meanings: used in 猙獰|狰狞[zheng1 ning2]

components.note: 犭 (dog, beast) — 狰 describes something fierce or savage-looking, as in a monstrous face.
争 (zhēng) gives an exact match for 狰's reading.

example.hanzi: 面具上画着一副狰狞的表情。
example.pinyin: Miànjù shàng huà zhe yí fù zhēngníng de biǎoqíng.
example.english: The mask was painted with a fierce, ferocious expression.
example.fact: 狰狞 (zhēngníng) describes a fierce, menacing appearance often used for monster masks or angry expressions — both characters share the dog radical 犭, historically used for beast-like or savage imagery.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 楣 names a wooden crossbeam above a door or gate.
眉 (méi) gives an exact match for 楣's reading.

example.hanzi: 门楣上挂着一块写有吉祥话的匾。
example.pinyin: Ménméi shàng guà zhe yí kuài xiě yǒu jíxiáng huà de biǎn.
example.english: A plaque with auspicious words hangs above the door's lintel.
example.fact: 门楣 (the door lintel) carried great symbolic weight in traditional Chinese homes, and the phrase 光耀门楣 ('to bring glory to the family's lintel') still means to bring honor to one's family.

meanings: to smooth or arrange sth using one's fingers
etymologyHint: To take 扌 a handful 寽; 寽 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 捋 describes an action done with the fingers, such as stroking or gathering something up.
寽 (lǜ) is very close to 捋's reading — same base sound, different tone — and 寽 itself depicts a handful clutched in the hand, matching 捋's sense of gathering something between the fingers.

example.hanzi: 老人一边思考,一边捋着胡子。
example.pinyin: Lǎorén yìbiān sīkǎo, yìbiān lǚ zhe húzi.
example.english: The old man stroked his beard while thinking.
example.fact: 捋胡子 (lǚ húzi, 'to stroke one's beard') is a classic gesture in Chinese storytelling and opera used to depict a wise, contemplative elder.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 涓 names a small stream or trickle of water.
肙 (yuàn) shares 涓's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 涓涓细流最终汇成了大江大河。
example.pinyin: Juānjuān xìliú zuìzhōng huìchéng le dà jiāng dà hé.
example.english: Trickling little streams eventually converge into great rivers.
example.fact: 涓涓细流 ('trickling little streams') is a common metaphor for how small, steady contributions — of effort, savings, or kindness — can accumulate into something much greater.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 荪 names a fragrant plant, a type of iris.
孙 (sūn) gives an exact match for 荪's reading.

example.hanzi: 荪是古代诗词中常见的香草名。
example.pinyin: Sūn shì gǔdài shīcí zhōng chángjiàn de xiāngcǎo míng.
example.english: Sun is a fragrant plant name commonly seen in ancient Chinese poetry.
example.fact: In the Chu Ci (楚辞), the ancient poetic anthology partly attributed to Qu Yuan, fragrant plants like 荪 were often used as metaphors for a virtuous ruler or a cherished ideal, a convention known as 'fragrant plants and beautiful people' symbolism.

meanings: one of the 28 lunar mansions in Chinese astronomy
etymologyHint: A woman 女 looking up at a star 米

components.note: 女 (woman) — part of the character's ideographic image of a woman.
米 here doesn't mean 'rice' — in 娄's ancient form it depicted stars or ornaments above a woman's head, tied to the character's use naming one of the 28 lunar mansions in Chinese astronomy.

example.hanzi: 娄宿是中国古代天文学中二十八宿之一。
example.pinyin: Lóuxiù shì Zhōngguó gǔdài tiānwénxué zhōng èrshíbā xiù zhī yī.
example.english: Lou is one of the 28 lunar mansions in ancient Chinese astronomy.
example.fact: The 28 lunar mansions (二十八宿) were a traditional Chinese system for dividing the sky along the moon's monthly path, used for astrology and calendar-keeping — 娄 names one of them.

components.note: 鹿 (deer) — 麝 names a small deer species known for producing musk.
射 (shè) gives an exact match for 麝's reading.

example.hanzi: 麝香是从雄性麝的腺体中提取的珍贵香料。
example.pinyin: Shèxiāng shì cóng xióngxìng shè de xiàntǐ zhōng tíqǔ de zhēnguì xiāngliào.
example.english: Musk is a precious fragrance extracted from the glands of the male musk deer.
example.fact: Musk deer are hunted for the musk pod in males, historically among the most valuable animal products by weight, which drove severe overhunting; all musk deer species are now protected, and most perfume musk today is synthetic.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — 蚤 names a flea.
叉 (chā) no longer resembles 蚤's modern reading zǎo — the sound has drifted apart over time, though it's traditionally treated as the phonetic component.

example.hanzi: 周末我们去逛了跳蚤市场。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù guàng le tiàozǎo shìchǎng.
example.english: On the weekend we went to browse the flea market.
example.fact: 跳蚤市场 ('flea market') is a direct calque of the Western term, thought to originate from 19th-century Paris markets selling secondhand goods, where fleas were jokingly said to infest the old furniture and clothing on sale.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 薰 names a fragrant herb, historically burned for its smoke.
熏 (xūn) gives an exact match for 薰's reading.

example.hanzi: 古人常用薰草驱除蚊虫。
example.pinyin: Gǔrén cháng yòng xūncǎo qūchú wénchóng.
example.english: Ancient people often burned fragrant herbs to drive away mosquitoes.
example.fact: 薰 is closely related to 熏 (xūn, 'to smoke, fumigate') — both describe using fragrant smoke, historically burning aromatic herbs not only for a pleasant scent but to repel insects, a practice recorded in classical Chinese texts.

components.note: 酉 (wine, alcohol) — 醮 names a ritual ceremony involving offerings of wine.
焦 (jiāo) is close to 醮's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 道士们在庭院里设醮祈福。
example.pinyin: Dàoshimen zài tíngyuàn lǐ shè jiào qífú.
example.english: The Daoist priests set up a ritual ceremony in the courtyard to pray for blessings.
example.fact: 醮 names a formal Daoist ritual involving offerings of wine and food to deities, still performed today at temple festivals in Taiwan and parts of southern China to pray for community blessings.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 搪 describes physically warding off or fending something away.
唐 (táng) gives an exact match for 搪's reading.

example.hanzi: 他随便找了个理由搪塞过去。
example.pinyin: Tā suíbiàn zhǎo le gè lǐyóu tángsè guòqù.
example.english: He casually found an excuse to brush the matter off.
example.fact: 搪塞 (tángsè) describes giving a vague, careless excuse just to avoid dealing with something properly — a common criticism in Chinese for insincere or halfhearted responses to a request.

components.note: 讠 (speech, words) — here linked to stillness in the sense of a hushed, unspoken calm.
必 (bì) shares 谧's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 夜晚的山谷显得格外静谧。
example.pinyin: Yèwǎn de shāngǔ xiǎnde géwài jìngmì.
example.english: At night, the valley seemed especially calm and quiet.
example.fact: 静谧 (jìngmì) is a favored literary word for peaceful stillness, often used in descriptive writing about nature at night — more evocative and poetic than the plain 安静 ('quiet').

etymologyHint: A dammed 垔 stream 氵; 垔 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 氵 (water) — 湮 relates to water sinking, being buried, or silting up.

垔 (yīn) partially resembles 湮's modern reading yān — same initial consonant, different final — matching its traditional role as this character's sound-indicating element, which itself originally depicted a dammed stream.

example.hanzi: 许多古代文明的痕迹早已湮灭在历史长河中。
example.pinyin: Xǔduō gǔdài wénmíng de hénjì zǎoyǐ yānmiè zài lìshǐ chánghé zhōng.
example.english: Traces of many ancient civilizations have long since vanished into the flow of history.
example.fact: 湮灭 (yānmiè) is also the standard Chinese physics term for particle-antiparticle 'annihilation' — as when an electron and a positron collide and convert entirely into energy — extending the character's older sense of sinking away and disappearing without a trace.

components.note: 车 (cart, vehicle) — 辍 originally described a cart stopping partway, extended to stopping any activity before completion.
叕 (zhuó) shares 辍's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 由于家庭贫困,他不得不辍学去工作。
example.pinyin: Yóuyú jiātíng pínkùn, tā bùdébù chuòxué qù gōngzuò.
example.english: Because his family was poor, he had no choice but to drop out of school and go to work.
example.fact: 辍学 ('to drop out of school') is a term frequently used in discussions of China's rural education policy — the Hope Project (希望工程), launched in 1989, was created specifically to fund schooling for children at risk of dropping out due to poverty.

components.note: 目 (eye) — 瞌 describes the eyes drooping shut from drowsiness.
盍 (hé) shares 瞌's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 上课时他总是打瞌睡。
example.pinyin: Shàngkè shí tā zǒngshì dǎ kēshuì.
example.english: He always dozes off during class.
example.fact: 打瞌睡 ('to doze off') is the everyday phrase for briefly nodding off while trying to stay awake, distinct from 睡觉 (shuìjiào), the general verb for sleeping properly.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 梆 names a hollow wooden clapper or rattle.
邦 (bāng) gives an exact match for 梆's reading.

example.hanzi: 以前,巡夜人会敲梆子提醒大家小心火烛。
example.pinyin: Yǐqián, xúnyèrén huì qiāo bāngzi tíxǐng dàjiā xiǎoxīn huǒzhú.
example.english: In the past, night watchmen would strike a wooden clapper to remind everyone to be careful with fire.
example.fact: 梆子 (bāngzi), a hollow wooden clapper struck to keep rhythm, gives its name to 梆子戏, one of China's major regional opera styles, named for the sharp, percussive clacking of this wooden instrument keeping the beat.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 樟 names the camphor tree.
章 (zhāng) gives an exact match for 樟's reading.

example.hanzi: 樟树的木材散发出一种特殊的香气,可以防虫。
example.pinyin: Zhāngshù de mùcái sànfā chū yì zhǒng tèshū de xiāngqì, kěyǐ fángchóng.
example.english: Camphor wood gives off a distinctive fragrance that can repel insects.
example.fact: Camphor extracted from the camphor tree (樟树) was historically one of Taiwan's most important export products in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, used worldwide in mothballs, medicine, and early plastics like celluloid.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 茉 names jasmine, in the compound 茉莉.
末 (mò) gives an exact match for 茉's reading.

example.hanzi: 茉莉花茶是中国最受欢迎的花茶之一。
example.pinyin: Mòlìhuā chá shì Zhōngguó zuì shòu huānyíng de huāchá zhī yī.
example.english: Jasmine tea is one of the most popular flower teas in China.
example.fact: The folk song 茉莉花 ('Jasmine Flower') is one of the most famous Chinese melodies worldwide — Puccini used its tune in his opera Turandot, and it was played during medal ceremonies at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.

meanings: used in 崎嶇|崎岖[qi2 qu1]

components.note: 山 (mountain) — 岖 describes rugged, uneven terrain.
区 (qū) gives an exact match for 岖's reading.

example.hanzi: 这条山路崎岖不平,开车要格外小心。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo shānlù qíqū bùpíng, kāichē yào géwài xiǎoxīn.
example.english: This mountain road is rugged and uneven, so you need to drive extra carefully.
example.fact: 崎岖 (qíqū) describes rough, uneven terrain and is very often used figuratively for a difficult, winding path in life or a career, as in 崎岖的人生道路 ('a rugged road through life').

etymologyHint: A mortar used to grind out powders

example.hanzi: 人的口腔后部长着臼齿,用来磨碎食物。
example.pinyin: Rén de kǒuqiāng hòubù zhǎng zhe jiùchǐ, yòng lái mósuì shíwù.
example.english: At the back of the mouth, humans have molars, used to grind up food.
example.fact: 臼齿 (jiùchǐ, 'mortar teeth') is the Chinese term for molars, named because their broad, ridged grinding surface works like a mortar (臼) crushing grain against a pestle.

components.note: 疒 (sickness, ailment) — 癣 names a skin condition, ringworm.
鲜 (xiān) shares 癣's initial sound but not the full syllable — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 潮湿的环境容易让人得皮肤癣。
example.pinyin: Cháoshī de huánjìng róngyì ràng rén dé pífū xuǎn.
example.english: A damp environment can easily lead to ringworm and other skin fungal infections.
example.fact: Despite its name, 癣 (ringworm) is not caused by a worm at all but by a fungal infection — the name comes from the ring-shaped rash the fungus often produces on the skin.

components.note: 禾 (grain plant) — 穑 describes harvesting grain.
啬 (sè) gives an exact match for 穑's reading.

example.hanzi: 古人常用稼穑来泛指农业劳动。
example.pinyin: Gǔrén cháng yòng jiàsè lái fànzhǐ nóngyè láodòng.
example.english: Ancient people often used the term 'sowing and reaping' to refer broadly to agricultural labor.
example.fact: 稼穑 (jiàsè) pairs 稼 ('to sow') with 穑 ('to reap'), forming a classical compound for farming as a whole that appears in the Book of Documents (尚书).

components.note: 王 (here the 玉 radical, 'jade') — 玷 originally described a flaw or blemish in a piece of jade.
占 (zhàn) no longer resembles 玷's modern reading diàn — the sound has drifted apart over time, though it's traditionally treated as the phonetic component.

example.hanzi: 他的贪污行为玷污了整个团队的名誉。
example.pinyin: Tā de tānwū xíngwéi diànwū le zhěnggè tuánduì de míngyù.
example.english: His corrupt behavior tarnished the whole team's reputation.
example.fact: 玷污 ('to tarnish') keeps alive the character's original image of a flaw or stain marring an otherwise flawless piece of jade — jade being one of the most prized and symbolically 'pure' materials in Chinese culture.

components.note: 饣 (food) — 馍 names a type of steamed or baked bread, common in northern China.
莫 (mò) is close to 馍's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 陕西人喜欢吃肉夹馍。
example.pinyin: Shǎnxī rén xǐhuan chī ròu jiā mó.
example.english: People in Shaanxi like to eat rougamo, meat sandwiched in flatbread.
example.fact: 肉夹馍, often called 'the Chinese hamburger,' is a Shaanxi specialty of stewed, chopped meat stuffed inside a crusty flatbread (馍) and has become popular internationally in recent years.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 呷 relates to sounds or actions made with the mouth, including sipping and, in reduplicated form, a quacking sound.
甲 (jiǎ) no longer resembles 呷's reading gā — the sound has drifted apart over time, though it's traditionally treated as the phonetic component.

example.hanzi: 鸭子呷呷地叫着,跟在鸭妈妈后面走。
example.pinyin: Yāzi gāgā de jiào zhe, gēn zài yā māma hòumiàn zǒu.
example.english: The ducklings quacked and quacked, following behind their mother.
example.fact: 呷呷 (gāgā) is one of several Chinese onomatopoeias for duck calls, alongside 嘎嘎 — Chinese, like many languages, has a rich set of dedicated sound words for different animal calls.

meanings: the stem and calyx of a flower

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 萼 names the calyx, the leaf-like part beneath a flower's petals.
咢 (è) gives an exact match for 萼's reading.

example.hanzi: 花萼是保护花朵未开放时的绿色部分。
example.pinyin: Huā è shì bǎohù huāduǒ wèi kāifàng shí de lǜsè bùfen.
example.english: The calyx is the green part that protects a flower before it blooms.
example.fact: 花萼 (the calyx), the ring of small leaf-like sepals beneath a flower's petals, protects the developing bud and is one of the four basic parts of a flower taught in botany, alongside the petals, stamens, and pistil.

meanings: used in 嫵媚|妩媚[wu3 mei4]

components.note: 女 (woman) — 妩 describes a charming, alluring quality, most often used of women.
无 (wú) is close to 妩's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 她笑起来的样子十分妩媚。
example.pinyin: Tā xiào qǐlái de yàngzi shífēn wǔmèi.
example.english: She looks very charming when she smiles.
example.fact: 妩媚 (wǔmèi) specifically describes a captivating, charming allure, most often used to compliment a woman's smile or bearing — both characters in the word share the 女 (woman) radical.

meanings: to stand for a long time
to stand for a long time (variant of 佇|伫[zhu4])

example.hanzi: 他伫立在窗前,望着远方的山。
example.pinyin: Tā zhùlì zài chuāng qián, wàng zhe yuǎnfāng de shān.
example.english: He stood for a long time by the window, gazing at the distant mountains.
example.fact: 伫立 (zhùlì) is a literary verb for standing still for a long stretch of time, often used in poetry and fiction to suggest quiet contemplation, longing, or waiting.

components.note: 丹 (cinnabar red) — 彤 describes a bright red or vermilion color.
彡 (shān) no longer resembles 彤's modern reading tóng — the sound has drifted apart over time, though it's traditionally treated as the phonetic component.

example.hanzi: 傍晚,天边泛起一片彤云。
example.pinyin: Bàngwǎn, tiānbiān fàn qǐ yí piàn tóngyún.
example.english: At dusk, red-tinted clouds spread across the horizon.
example.fact: 彤 is a common character in Chinese given names, chosen for its bright, warm meaning of vermilion red — a color traditionally associated with good fortune and vitality in Chinese culture.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 莓 names low, soft-fruited plants such as berries and moss.
每 (měi) is close to 莓's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 草莓是很多孩子最喜欢的水果。
example.pinyin: Cǎoméi shì hěn duō háizi zuì xǐhuan de shuǐguǒ.
example.english: Strawberries are many children's favorite fruit.
example.fact: 莓 appears in the names of many berries in Chinese — 草莓 (strawberry), 蓝莓 (blueberry), 黑莓 (blackberry) — since it originally referred to small, soft, seed-covered fruits and moss-like low plants.

components.note: 山 (mountain) — 岬 names a landform, a cape or headland jutting into the sea.
甲 (jiǎ) gives an exact match for 岬's reading.

example.hanzi: 这个岬角是观赏日出的绝佳地点。
example.pinyin: Zhège jiǎjiǎo shì guānshǎng rìchū de jué jiā dìdiǎn.
example.english: This headland is a fantastic spot for watching the sunrise.
example.fact: A 岬角 (cape or headland) is a point of land projecting into the sea, often formed as softer surrounding rock erodes away faster than the harder rock of the point itself.

meanings: used in 嬋媛|婵媛[chan2 yuan2]

components.note: 女 (woman) — 媛 describes a beautiful, accomplished woman.
爰 (yuán) is close to 媛's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 她出身名门,是上海知名的名媛。
example.pinyin: Tā chūshēn míngmén, shì Shànghǎi zhīmíng de míngyuàn.
example.english: She comes from a prominent family and is a well-known socialite in Shanghai.
example.fact: 名媛 (míngyuàn), often translated 'socialite,' historically described a woman of good family and refined accomplishments; in 1930s Shanghai it named the fashionable, Western-educated women prominent in the city's high society.

components.note: 忄 (heart, emotion) — 惆 describes a feeling of wistful sadness or disappointment.
周 (zhōu) shares 惆's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 看着老照片,他心中涌起一丝惆怅。
example.pinyin: Kànzhe lǎo zhàopiàn, tā xīnzhōng yǒngqǐ yì sī chóuchàng.
example.english: Looking at the old photos, a trace of wistful sadness rose in his heart.
example.fact: 惆怅 (chóuchàng) describes a gentle, lingering melancholy — often triggered by nostalgia or disappointment — and is a favorite mood-word in classical Chinese poetry for bittersweet reflection.

components.note: 鱼 (fish) — 鳎 names a flatfish, the sole.

example.hanzi: 舌鳎是一种扁平的海鱼,常用来做菜。
example.pinyin: Shétǎ shì yì zhǒng biǎnpíng de hǎiyú, cháng yòng lái zuò cài.
example.english: Sole is a flat sea fish that is often cooked as food.
example.fact: Sole are flatfish born symmetrical that undergo a strange transformation as juveniles: one eye migrates across the head to join the other, so the adult fish can lie flat on the seabed with both eyes facing upward.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 啾 describes chirping or high-pitched crying sounds.
秋 (qiū) shares 啾's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 林间传来鸟儿啁啾的叫声。
example.pinyin: Lín jiān chuánlái niǎo'er zhōujiū de jiào shēng.
example.english: The chirping calls of birds drifted from the woods.
example.fact: 啁啾 (zhōujiū) is a classical onomatopoeia imitating the chirping of small birds, appearing frequently in Tang and Song dynasty poetry to evoke a lively, peaceful natural scene.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 囔 describes indistinct muttering.
囊 (náng) is close to 囔's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 他嘴里嘟囔囔地说了些什么,我没听清。
example.pinyin: Tā zuǐ lǐ dūnāngnang de shuō le xiē shénme, wǒ méi tīngqīng.
example.english: He muttered something under his breath, but I couldn't quite hear it.
example.fact: 嘟囔 (dūnang) describes muttering complaints or unclear words under one's breath, usually implying mild grumbling rather than a clear statement.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — 蜓 names an insect, used in 蜻蜓 (dragonfly).
廷 (tíng) gives an exact match for 蜓's reading.

example.hanzi: 蜻蜓的幼虫生活在水里,叫做水虿。
example.pinyin: Qīngtíng de yòuchóng shēnghuó zài shuǐ lǐ, jiàozuò shuǐchài.
example.english: Dragonfly larvae live in the water and are called naiads.
example.fact: Dragonfly larvae, called naiads, can live underwater for years before finally emerging and molting into their winged adult form — a striking metamorphosis from an aquatic predator into an aerial one.

components.note: 子 (child) — 孺 names a young child.
需 (xū) shares 孺's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 这场救援行动让妇孺老弱都得到了安置。
example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng jiùyuán xíngdòng ràng fùrú lǎoruò dōu dédào le ānzhì.
example.english: This rescue operation ensured that women, children, and the elderly were all taken care of.
example.fact: 妇孺 ('women and children') appears in the common expression 妇孺皆知 ('known even to women and children'), meaning something is common knowledge understood by absolutely everyone.

meanings: to be swayed by (personal considerations etc)

components.note: 彳 (step, walking) — 徇 originally related to following or going along with something, extended to being swayed by personal interest.
旬 (xún) is close to 徇's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 作为法官,他从不徇私舞弊。
example.pinyin: Zuòwéi fǎguān, tā cóng bù xùnsī wǔbì.
example.english: As a judge, he never shows favoritism or engages in corrupt practices.
example.fact: 徇私 (xùnsī) describes bending rules or abusing one's position for personal or family benefit — a frequent term in Chinese anti-corruption and legal reporting, as in 徇私枉法 ('bending the law for personal gain').

components.note: 彳 (step, walking) — 徵 relates to summoning someone to come and serve.
正 (zhèng) is close to 徵's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 古代朝廷常常徵召各地贤才入仕。
example.pinyin: Gǔdài cháotíng chángcháng zhēngzhào gèdì xiáncái rùshì.
example.english: Ancient imperial courts often summoned talented people from all over to serve in office.
example.fact: 徵 is the traditional, more formal form of 征 in the sense 'to summon or recruit'; it also names one of the five notes of the ancient Chinese pentatonic scale (宫商角徵羽), though that musical sense is read with a different tone, zhǐ, not zhēng.

meanings: to weld; to braze; to solder

components.note: 火 (fire) — 焊 describes joining metal using intense heat.
旱 (hàn) gives an exact match for 焊's reading.

example.hanzi: 工人正在用电焊机焊接钢铁部件。
example.pinyin: Gōngrén zhèngzài yòng diànhànjī hànjiē gāngtiě bùjiàn.
example.english: The worker is using an electric welder to weld steel parts together.
example.fact: Modern arc welding, which uses an electric current to melt and join metal, was developed in the late 19th century and remains one of the most important manufacturing techniques for everything from skyscrapers to car bodies.

meanings: one of the Five Sacred Mountains in China

components.note: 山 (mountain) — 岱 names Mount Tai, one of China's Five Sacred Mountains.
代 (dài) gives an exact match for 岱's reading.

example.hanzi: 泰山又被称为岱宗,是五岳之首。
example.pinyin: Tàishān yòu bèi chēng wéi Dàizōng, shì wǔyuè zhī shǒu.
example.english: Mount Tai is also called Daizong, and is foremost among the Five Sacred Mountains.
example.fact: Mount Tai (泰山), also known as 岱宗, has been a site of imperial sacrifice for over two thousand years — emperors historically climbed it to perform the 封禅 ritual, reporting their achievements to heaven and earth.

components.note: 日 is 昵's official radical, though the connection is more classificatory than meaning-based — 昵 describes emotional closeness, not anything related to the sun.
尼 (ní) is close to 昵's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 朋友们都用一个可爱的昵称叫她。
example.pinyin: Péngyoumen dōu yòng yí gè kě'ài de nìchēng jiào tā.
example.english: Her friends all call her by a cute nickname.
example.fact: 昵称 (nìchēng, 'nickname') is the standard modern Chinese word for a nickname or online username, used everywhere from chat apps to social media profile settings.

etymologyHint: Three tally marks; compare ten 十 and twenty 廿

components.note: 卅 packs three tally strokes (visually similar to 川) into one character for 'thirty' — compare the single stroke of 十 (ten) and the two strokes of 廿 (twenty).

example.hanzi: 这篇文章写于建国卅周年之际。
example.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng xiěyú jiànguó sà zhōunián zhī jì.
example.english: This article was written on the occasion of the 30th anniversary of the nation's founding.
example.fact: 卅 (sà, 'thirty') belongs to a small set of classical Chinese numeral characters — alongside 廿 (niàn, 'twenty') and 卌 (xì, 'forty') — that compress a two-character number into a single glyph, once common in formal writing and inscriptions.

etymologyHint: Storm 猋 winds 风; 猋 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 风 (wind) — 飙 names a violent, storm-force wind.
猋 (biāo, 'a pack of ferocious dogs; a storm') is an exact match for 飙's reading — 猋 itself is built from three dogs 犬, evoking a wild, gale-like fury.

example.hanzi: 最近这个城市的房价一路飙升。
example.pinyin: Zuìjìn zhège chéngshì de fángjià yílù biāoshēng.
example.english: Recently, housing prices in this city have skyrocketed.
example.fact: 飙升 ('to skyrocket') extends 飙's original sense of a violent gale into modern usage for anything rising fast and dramatically, whether prices, temperatures, or statistics.

components.note: 阝 (here the 邑 radical, 'settlement, place') — 邙 is used only in the mountain and place name 北邙.
亡 (wáng) shares 邙's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 北邙山自古就是洛阳附近著名的墓葬之地。
example.pinyin: Běimángshān zìgǔ jiùshì Luòyáng fùjìn zhùmíng de mùzàng zhī dì.
example.english: Mount Beimang has long been a famous burial ground near Luoyang.
example.fact: Mount Beimang, just north of the ancient capital Luoyang, became one of China's most famous burial grounds — a Tang-dynasty line, 'live in Suzhou and Hangzhou, be buried at Beimang,' reflects its long-standing reputation as a resting place for emperors and elites.

components.note: 疒 (sickness, ailment) — 痞 originally named a medical condition, an abdominal lump, later extended to describe a rascally, unsavory character.
否 (fǒu) no longer resembles 痞's modern reading pǐ — the sound has drifted apart over time, though it's traditionally treated as the phonetic component.

example.hanzi: 他一身痞气,说话总是很不正经。
example.pinyin: Tā yìshēn pǐqì, shuōhuà zǒngshì hěn bú zhèngjing.
example.english: He has a rascally air about him and never speaks seriously.
example.fact: 痞子 ('hoodlum, rascal') gave its name to a whole literary genre in 1990s China called 痞子文学 ('hoodlum literature'), pioneered by writer Wang Shuo, known for cynical, streetwise characters and slang-heavy dialogue.

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — 隼 names a falcon, a bird of prey.
十 (shí) no longer resembles 隼's modern reading sǔn — the sound has drifted apart over time, though it's traditionally treated as the phonetic component.

example.hanzi: 隼是一种飞行速度极快的猛禽。
example.pinyin: Sǔn shì yì zhǒng fēixíng sùdù jíkuài de měngqín.
example.english: The falcon is a bird of prey capable of extremely fast flight.
example.fact: The peregrine falcon (游隼), a close relative named with this character, is the fastest animal on Earth, reaching speeds over 320 km/h (200 mph) in a hunting dive.

components.note: 忄 (heart, emotion) — 恫 relates to fear or distress, as in intimidation.
同 (tóng) shares 恫's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 警方指出,这封信带有明显的恫吓性质。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhǐchū, zhè fēng xìn dài yǒu míngxiǎn de dònghè xìngzhì.
example.english: Police pointed out that this letter clearly had an intimidating nature.
example.fact: 恫吓 ('to intimidate, to threaten') combines 恫 (fear, distress) with 吓 (to scare), and is the standard word used in Chinese news reports for verbal threats or intimidation tactics.

components.note: 忄 (heart, emotion) — 怆 describes deep sorrow or grief.
仓 (cāng) no longer resembles 怆's modern reading chuàng — the sound has drifted apart over time, though it's traditionally treated as the phonetic component.

example.hanzi: 这部电影的结局让观众感到无比悲怆。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng de jiéjú ràng guānzhòng gǎndào wúbǐ bēichuàng.
example.english: The film's ending left the audience feeling deeply sorrowful.
example.fact: 悲怆 (bēichuàng) is the standard Chinese translation for 'pathétique,' as in Beethoven's Piano Sonata No. 8, known in Chinese as 悲怆奏鸣曲, and Tchaikovsky's Symphony No. 6.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 桀 originally described a chicken roost made of wood, before being borrowed as the name of the tyrant King Jie.

example.hanzi: 夏桀是中国历史上有名的暴君。
example.pinyin: Xià Jié shì Zhōngguó lìshǐ shàng yǒumíng de bàojūn.
example.english: King Jie of Xia is a famous tyrant in Chinese history.
example.fact: King Jie was the last ruler of the semi-legendary Xia dynasty, remembered in Chinese historical tradition as a cruel tyrant overthrown by Tang of Shang — his name became a byword for despotism, as in the phrase 助桀为虐 ('helping Jie do evil').

meanings: silk ribbon attached as a seal

components.note: 纟 (thread, silk) — 绶 names a silk cord or ribbon, historically used to attach an official seal.
受 (shòu) gives an exact match for 绶's reading.

example.hanzi: 获奖选手胸前佩戴着绶带。
example.pinyin: Huòjiǎng xuǎnshǒu xiōngqián pèidài zhe shòudài.
example.english: The award-winning contestant wore a sash across their chest.
example.fact: 绶带 (shòudài) is the modern Chinese word for the ceremonial sash worn by pageant winners, medal recipients, or officials — a modern extension of its ancient use as a silk cord attaching an official seal of rank.

meanings: seat of a pair of trousers

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — 裆 names the crotch section of a pair of pants.
当 (dāng) gives an exact match for 裆's reading.

example.hanzi: 裤子的裤裆破了一个洞。
example.pinyin: Kùzi de kùdāng pò le yí gè dòng.
example.english: There's a hole torn in the crotch of the pants.
example.fact: 裤裆 (kùdāng) names the crotch section of a pair of pants — the character 裆 combines the clothing radical 衤 with 当, here indicating the part of the garment positioned between the legs.

components.note: 皿 (dish, vessel) — 盂 names a wide, open bowl or basin.
于 (yú) gives an exact match for 盂's reading.

example.hanzi: 以前很多家庭都会在屋里放一个痰盂。
example.pinyin: Yǐqián hěnduō jiātíng dōu huì zài wū lǐ fàng yí gè tányú.
example.english: In the past, many households would keep a spittoon in the house.
example.fact: 痰盂 (the spittoon) was once a common fixture in Chinese homes and public spaces, reflecting a widespread traditional habit that public health campaigns have worked for decades to discourage.

meanings: used in 秦檜|秦桧[Qin2 Hui4]

components.note: 木 (tree) — 桧 names a type of juniper or cypress tree.
会 (huì) shares 桧's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 秦桧是中国历史上臭名昭著的奸臣。
example.pinyin: Qín Huì shì Zhōngguó lìshǐ shàng chòumíng zhāozhù de jiānchén.
example.english: Qin Hui is a notoriously infamous treacherous official in Chinese history.
example.fact: Qin Hui, a Southern Song dynasty chancellor, is remembered as one of history's greatest villains for engineering the execution of the loyal general Yue Fei — kneeling statues of Qin Hui and his wife still stand outside Yue Fei's temple in Hangzhou.

components.note: 虫 (insect, worm) — 蚓 names the earthworm.
引 (yǐn) gives an exact match for 蚓's reading.

example.hanzi: 蚯蚓能帮助疏松土壤,对农业很有益。
example.pinyin: Qiūyǐn néng bāngzhù shūsōng tǔrǎng, duì nóngyè hěn yǒuyì.
example.english: Earthworms help loosen the soil and are very beneficial for agriculture.
example.fact: Charles Darwin spent the last years of his life studying earthworms, concluding in his final book (1881) that their ceaseless burrowing had shaped the very structure of the soil across entire landscapes.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 抠 describes picking, scraping, or digging at something with the fingers.
区 (qū) no longer resembles 抠's modern reading kōu — the sound has drifted apart over time, though it's traditionally treated as the phonetic component.

example.hanzi: 他花钱特别抠门,从不乱花一分钱。
example.pinyin: Tā huāqián tèbié kōumén, cóng bú luàn huā yì fēn qián.
example.english: He's extremely stingy with money and never spends a cent carelessly.
example.fact: 抠门 (kōumén) is a lively colloquial word for being stingy, literally evoking someone who would 'pick and scrape' at every last coin — one of many vivid body-action metaphors in spoken Mandarin for personality traits.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 嗷 describes a loud crying or wailing sound.
敖 (áo) gives an exact match for 嗷's reading.

example.hanzi: 灾区的孩子们嗷嗷待哺,急需援助。
example.pinyin: Zāiqū de háizimen áo'áo dàibǔ, jíxū yuánzhù.
example.english: The children in the disaster area are crying out to be fed and urgently need help.
example.fact: 嗷嗷待哺, literally 'crying out, waiting to be fed,' originally described baby birds crying for food in the nest and is now used for anyone helplessly dependent and urgently in need.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 槌 names a wooden mallet or hammer.
追 (zhuī) shares 槌's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 鼓手用鼓槌用力敲击大鼓。
example.pinyin: Gǔshǒu yòng gǔchuí yònglì qiāojī dàgǔ.
example.english: The drummer struck the big drum hard with drum mallets.
example.fact: 槌 specifically names a wooden mallet, as in 鼓槌 (drumstick) or 木槌 (a wooden gavel), distinguishing it from the metal-headed 锤, which shares a similar sound and meaning but a different material.

components.note: 疒 (sickness, ailment) — 痘 names skin eruptions, from smallpox pustules to ordinary pimples.
豆 (dòu) gives an exact match for 痘's reading.

example.hanzi: 青春期长痘痘是很常见的现象。
example.pinyin: Qīngchūnqī zhǎng dòudou shì hěn chángjiàn de xiànxiàng.
example.english: Getting pimples during puberty is a very common phenomenon.
example.fact: Smallpox was historically called 痘 or 天花 in Chinese, and China developed some of the earliest forms of inoculation against it — a technique called 人痘接种 (variolation) — centuries before Edward Jenner's famous 1796 vaccine.

components.note: 疒 (sickness, ailment) — 痢 names an intestinal illness, dysentery.
利 (lì) gives an exact match for 痢's reading.

example.hanzi: 在卫生条件差的地区,痢疾曾是常见的疾病。
example.pinyin: Zài wèishēng tiáojiàn chà de dìqū, lìji céng shì chángjiàn de jíbìng.
example.english: In areas with poor sanitation, dysentery was once a common disease.
example.fact: Dysentery spreads through contaminated food and water, and improving sanitation and clean water access — rather than medicine alone — has historically been the single most effective way to reduce its incidence worldwide.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 芮 originally described small grass sprouts, before becoming mainly a surname and place name.
内 (nèi) no longer resembles 芮's modern reading ruì — the sound has drifted apart over time, though it's traditionally treated as the phonetic component.

example.hanzi: 芮是一个不太常见的姓氏。
example.pinyin: Ruì shì yí gè bú tài chángjiàn de xìngshì.
example.english: Rui is a relatively uncommon surname.
example.fact: 芮 is primarily encountered today as a surname or in given names, tracing back to the ancient state of Rui (芮国), a small vassal state during the Western Zhou dynasty in what is now Shaanxi province.

components.note: 虫 (insect, worm) — 蚣 names the centipede, in the compound 蜈蚣.
公 (gōng) gives an exact match for 蚣's reading.

example.hanzi: 翻开石头,下面藏着一条蜈蚣。
example.pinyin: Fānkāi shítou, xiàmiàn cáng zhe yì tiáo wúgōng.
example.english: Turning over the rock, a centipede was hiding underneath.
example.fact: Despite being called a 'hundred-legged bug' (百足虫) in Chinese, no centipede species actually has exactly 100 legs — the number of leg pairs is always odd, ranging from 15 pairs to as many as 191 pairs depending on the species.

etymologyHint: A bar 一 laid across a gate 门

components.note: 门 (gate, door) — 闩 depicts a barred door.
一 (one, a horizontal stroke) — depicts the bar laid across the gate to lock it.

example.hanzi: 晚上睡觉前,他会把门闩插好。
example.pinyin: Wǎnshang shuìjiào qián, tā huì bǎ ménshuān chā hǎo.
example.english: Before going to bed at night, he bolts the door latch shut.
example.fact: 门闩 (a door bolt) was the standard way to secure a traditional Chinese wooden door before modern locks became common — a sliding wooden or metal bar dropped into brackets on either side of the doorframe.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 铿 describes the clanging sound of struck metal.
坚 (jiān) no longer resembles 铿's modern reading kēng — the sound has drifted apart over time, though it's traditionally treated as the phonetic component.

example.hanzi: 他的演讲铿锵有力,赢得了满堂喝彩。
example.pinyin: Tā de yǎnjiǎng kēngqiāng yǒulì, yíngdé le mǎntáng hècǎi.
example.english: His speech was forceful and resounding, winning applause from the whole room.
example.fact: 铿锵有力 (kēngqiāng yǒulì) borrows the clanging sound of struck metal or bells to describe speech, music, or writing that is powerful, rhythmic, and resonant.

meanings: used in 颶風|飓风[ju4 feng1]

components.note: 风 (wind) — 飓 names a violent storm, a hurricane.
具 (jù) gives an exact match for 飓's reading.

example.hanzi: 飓风即将登陆,居民纷纷撤离。
example.pinyin: Jùfēng jíjiāng dēnglù, jūmín fēnfēn chèlí.
example.english: As the hurricane was about to make landfall, residents evacuated one after another.
example.fact: 飓风 specifically refers to tropical cyclones over the Atlantic and eastern Pacific ('hurricanes'), while the same kind of storm over the western Pacific, including near China, is instead called 台风 ('typhoon') — the same phenomenon named differently by ocean basin.

components.note: 疒 (sickness, ailment) — 疱 names a fluid-filled skin swelling, a blister.
包 (bāo) shares 疱's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 烫伤的地方起了一个水疱。
example.pinyin: Tàngshāng de dìfang qǐ le yí gè shuǐpào.
example.english: A blister formed on the burned skin.
example.fact: A blister forms when fluid accumulates beneath the outer layer of skin, usually as a protective cushion in response to friction, heat, or damage — the fluid itself is mostly plasma, the liquid component of blood.

components.note: 虫 (insect, worm) — used loosely here for a small aquatic creature; 蝌 names the tadpole, paired with 蚪.
科 (kē) gives an exact match for 蝌's reading.

example.hanzi: 蝌蚪长大后会变成青蛙。
example.pinyin: Kēdǒu zhǎngdà hòu huì biànchéng qīngwā.
example.english: Tadpoles grow up to become frogs.
example.fact: A tadpole's transformation into a frog is a dramatic metamorphosis: it must resorb its own tail for energy, grow four legs, and remodel its gills into lungs, all controlled by a surge of thyroid hormone.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — extended here to describe a body part sticking out or protruding, as with lips in a pout.
厥 (jué) is close to 撅's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 小女孩因为没买到玩具,撅着嘴生气。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo nǚhái yīnwèi méi mǎidào wánjù, juē zhe zuǐ shēngqì.
example.english: The little girl pouted angrily because she didn't get the toy.
example.fact: 撅嘴 (juēzuǐ, 'to pout') describes the universal childlike expression of sticking out one's lower lip in displeasure — a gesture Chinese parents and cartoons alike use as shorthand for a sulking child.

components.note: 虫 (insect, worm) — 蚯 names the earthworm, paired with 蚓.
丘 (qiū) gives an exact match for 蚯's reading.

example.hanzi: 花园里的泥土中生活着许多蚯蚓。
example.pinyin: Huāyuán lǐ de nítǔ zhōng shēnghuó zhe xǔduō qiūyǐn.
example.english: Many earthworms live in the soil of the garden.
example.fact: Earthworms breathe through their skin rather than lungs, which is why they must stay moist — if their skin dries out they can suffocate, which is why they surface most often after rain.

components.note: 斗 (here referring to the Big Dipper constellation) — 斡 originally described the wheeling motion of the Dipper around the pole star, giving rise to its meaning 'to turn, to rotate.'

example.hanzi: 两国之间的紧张关系需要第三方从中斡旋。
example.pinyin: Liǎng guó zhījiān de jǐnzhāng guānxi xūyào dì sān fāng cóngzhōng wòxuán.
example.english: The tense relationship between the two countries needs a third party to mediate.
example.fact: 斡旋 (wòxuán, 'to mediate') is standard diplomatic vocabulary in Chinese news media, frequently describing a third country or organization working behind the scenes to help resolve a conflict between others.

components.note: 穴 (cave, hole) — 窠 names a nest, den, or hollow.
果 (guǒ) no longer resembles 窠's modern reading kē — the sound has drifted apart over time, though it's traditionally treated as the phonetic component.

example.hanzi: 这部电影的叙事手法不落窠臼,令人耳目一新。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng de xùshì shǒufǎ bú luò kējiù, lìng rén ěrmù yīxīn.
example.english: This film's storytelling avoids conventional patterns and feels refreshingly original.
example.fact: 不落窠臼 (bú luò kējiù), literally 'not falling into the nest and mortar,' is a common compliment in Chinese art and literary criticism for a work that breaks free of tired, conventional patterns.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 荚 names the pod of a leguminous plant.
夹 (jiā) is close to 荚's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 妈妈在厨房里剥豆荚准备做晚饭。
example.pinyin: Māma zài chúfáng lǐ bāo dòujiá zhǔnbèi zuò wǎnfàn.
example.english: Mom is shelling bean pods in the kitchen to prepare dinner.
example.fact: Bean pods are botanically classified as legumes, one of the few plant families able to fix nitrogen from the air through bacteria living in their roots — which is why farmers often rotate legume crops to naturally enrich depleted soil.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — 耷 originally described large, drooping ears.
大 (dà) is close to 耷's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 小狗耷拉着耳朵,看起来很沮丧。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu dāla zhe ěrduo, kànqǐlái hěn jǔsàng.
example.english: The little dog's ears were drooping, and it looked dejected.
example.fact: 耷拉 (dāla) is a lively colloquial word for something drooping or hanging limply — used for a dog's ears, a person's eyelids, or someone's head hanging low in disappointment.

components.note: 石 (stone) — 砚 names a stone slab used for grinding ink.
见 (jiàn) no longer resembles 砚's modern reading yàn — the sound has drifted apart over time, though it's traditionally treated as the phonetic component.

example.hanzi: 笔、墨、纸、砚被称为文房四宝。
example.pinyin: Bǐ, mò, zhǐ, yàn bèi chēng wéi wénfáng sìbǎo.
example.english: The brush, ink, paper, and inkstone are called the Four Treasures of the Study.
example.fact: 砚 (the inkstone), on which a scholar grinds a solid ink stick with water to make liquid ink, is one of the 文房四宝 ('Four Treasures of the Study') essential to traditional Chinese calligraphy and painting.

etymologyHint: Flat 片 pages 片 of wood

components.note: 片 (a thin slice, plank) — 牒 originally referred to a thin wooden or bamboo slip used for writing before paper, hence its meaning 'document.'
枼 (yè) doesn't match 牒's reading dié on its own, but it's part of a phonetic family — 谍, 碟, 蝶 — that all carry a related 'dié' sound from the same root.

example.hanzi: 对方向我们发出了最后通牒。
example.pinyin: Duìfāng xiàng wǒmen fāchū le zuìhòu tōngdié.
example.english: The other side issued us an ultimatum.
example.fact: 最后通牒 (zuìhòu tōngdié, 'ultimatum') is standard diplomatic and news vocabulary — 牒, once meaning an official written notice, here names the final, non-negotiable communication sent before an escalation such as war or a lawsuit.

components.note: 贝 (money, valuables — originally cowrie shells) — 赈 describes distributing money or goods to people in need.
辰 (chén) shares 赈's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 地震发生后,政府立即展开赈灾工作。
example.pinyin: Dìzhèn fāshēng hòu, zhèngfǔ lìjí zhǎnkāi zhènzāi gōngzuò.
example.english: After the earthquake struck, the government immediately began disaster relief work.
example.fact: 赈灾 (zhènzāi, 'disaster relief') combines the money radical 贝 in 赈 with 灾 ('disaster'), reflecting the character's original meaning of distributing grain or funds to people affected by famine or flood.

etymologyHint: A warm 昫 fire 灬; 昫 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 煦 describes gentle warmth, as from sunlight.
昫 (xù) is an exact match for 煦's reading — 昫 itself is built from 日 (sun) and 句, and independently means 'warm.'

example.hanzi: 三月的阳光和煦,让人感到十分舒适。
example.pinyin: Sānyuè de yángguāng héxù, ràng rén gǎndào shífēn shūshì.
example.english: The March sunshine is warm and gentle, making people feel very comfortable.
example.fact: 和煦 (héxù) is a favorite word in Chinese weather and travel writing for describing mild, pleasantly warm sunshine, especially in spring — evoking comfort rather than the harsher heat implied by 炎热 ('scorching').

meanings: move the mouth as in speaking

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 嗫 describes hesitant, mumbling attempts to speak.
聂 (niè) gives an exact match for 嗫's reading.

example.hanzi: 他想说什么,却嗫嚅着没有说出口。
example.pinyin: Tā xiǎng shuō shénme, què nièrú zhe méiyǒu shuō chūkǒu.
example.english: He wanted to say something, but mumbled hesitantly and never got the words out.
example.fact: 嗫嚅 (nièrú) describes the halting, mumbling attempt to speak when someone is too nervous, embarrassed, or unsure to get their words out clearly.

components.note: 耒 (plow, farming tool) — 耙 names a rake or harrow used to break up soil.
巴 (bā) is close to 耙's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 农民用耙把土地耙平,准备播种。
example.pinyin: Nóngmín yòng bà bǎ tǔdì bà píng, zhǔnbèi bōzhòng.
example.english: Farmers use a rake to level the soil in preparation for planting.
example.fact: 耙 names both a farming tool for breaking up and leveling soil and the action of using it — modern mechanized rotary harrows have replaced hand and animal-drawn versions on most large farms today.

meanings: Rong, another name for Fuzhou 福州[Fu2 zhou1]

components.note: 木 (tree) — 榕 names the banyan tree.
容 (róng) gives an exact match for 榕's reading.

example.hanzi: 厦门是一座种满榕树的美丽城市。
example.pinyin: Xiàmén shì yí zuò zhòng mǎn róngshù de měilì chéngshì.
example.english: Xiamen is a beautiful city full of banyan trees.
example.fact: 榕 is Fuzhou's official city tree, giving Fuzhou its poetic nickname 榕城 ('Banyan City') — the trees' aerial roots let a single banyan grow to cover a huge area, sometimes forming what looks like an entire small forest from one trunk.

components.note: 革 (leather, hide) — historically linked to nomadic peoples associated with leather goods and horse gear.
达 (dá) gives an exact match for 鞑's reading.

example.hanzi: 鞑靼是历史上活跃于欧亚草原的游牧民族。
example.pinyin: Dádá shì lìshǐ shàng huóyuè yú Ōuyà cǎoyuán de yóumù mínzú.
example.english: The Tatars were a nomadic people historically active on the Eurasian steppe.
example.fact: 鞑靼 (Tatar) was historically used by Chinese sources as a broad term for various nomadic peoples of the northern steppe, and the name later gave rise to the English word 'Tartar' via Central Asian and European usage.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) is 袤's official radical, though the link is more structural than meaning-based — 袤 describes length or extent, not clothing.
矛 (máo) is close to 袤's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 广袤的草原一望无际。
example.pinyin: Guǎngmào de cǎoyuán yíwàng wújì.
example.english: The vast, boundless grassland stretches as far as the eye can see.
example.fact: 广袤 (guǎngmào) pairs 广 ('wide, east-west extent') with 袤 ('long, north-south extent') — together forming a classical way to describe a vast territory's full extent in both dimensions.

components.note: 讠 (speech, words) — 谌 originally described sincerity or trustworthiness in what one says.
甚 (shén) shares 谌's final sound but not its initial — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 谌是一个较为少见的姓氏,与常见的陈姓同音不同字。
example.pinyin: Chén shì yí gè jiào wéi shǎojiàn de xìngshì, yǔ chángjiàn de Chén xìng tóngyīn bù tóngzì.
example.english: Chen (谌) is a relatively uncommon surname, a homophone of but written differently from the common surname 陈.
example.fact: 谌 and the far more common surname 陈 are exact homophones but completely different characters and lineages — a reminder that Mandarin's limited set of syllables produces many surname homophones distinguished only in writing.

components.note: 酉 (wine, alcohol) — 醺 describes the state of being drunk or tipsy.
熏 (xūn) gives an exact match for 醺's reading.

example.hanzi: 喝了两杯红酒后,她感觉有点微醺。
example.pinyin: Hē le liǎng bēi hóngjiǔ hòu, tā gǎnjué yǒudiǎn wēixūn.
example.english: After two glasses of red wine, she felt a little tipsy.
example.fact: 微醺 (wēixūn, 'slightly tipsy') has become a popular marketing term in China in recent years, used to brand low-alcohol drinks and cocktails aimed at a relaxed, pleasant buzz rather than full intoxication.

etymologyHint: Dried 干 grain stalks 禾; 干 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 禾 (grain plant) — 秆 names the dried stalk left after harvesting grain.
干 (gàn) is close to 秆's reading gǎn — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 秋收后,农民常把秸秆用来做肥料。
example.pinyin: Qiūshōu hòu, nóngmín cháng bǎ jiēgǎn yòng lái zuò féiliào.
example.english: After the autumn harvest, farmers often use crop stalks as fertilizer.
example.fact: Burning leftover crop stalks in the fields was once common across rural China but is now restricted in many regions because of the severe air pollution it causes, pushing farmers toward alternatives like composting the straw into fertilizer.

components.note: 彳 (step, walking) — 徨 describes wandering or moving about aimlessly, without direction.
皇 (huáng) gives an exact match for 徨's reading.

example.hanzi: 面对人生的重大选择,他感到十分彷徨。
example.pinyin: Miànduì rénshēng de zhòngdà xuǎnzé, tā gǎndào shífēn pánghuáng.
example.english: Facing a major life choice, he felt completely lost and uncertain.
example.fact: 彷徨 is also the title of a 1926 short story collection by the influential writer Lu Xun, reflecting the disillusionment and uncertainty many Chinese intellectuals felt in the years following the 1911 revolution.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 橹 names a wooden oar or scull.
鲁 (lǔ) gives an exact match for 橹's reading.

example.hanzi: 船夫用力摇橹,小船缓缓前行。
example.pinyin: Chuánfū yònglì yáolǔ, xiǎochuán huǎnhuǎn qiánxíng.
example.english: The boatman rowed the scull hard, and the small boat slowly moved forward.
example.fact: Unlike a Western oar that is lifted and dipped, a traditional Chinese 橹 (scull) stays continuously in the water and is worked with a snake-like side-to-side motion — a technique still used on gondola-like boats in places like Suzhou's canals.

components.note: 羽 (feather, wings) — 翡 originally named the kingfisher bird, later borrowed for the green gemstone jadeite.
非 (fēi) is close to 翡's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 翡翠是中国传统文化中极受重视的玉石。
example.pinyin: Fěicuì shì Zhōngguó chuántǒng wénhuà zhōng jí shòu zhòngshì de yùshí.
example.english: Jadeite is a gemstone highly valued in traditional Chinese culture.
example.fact: 翡翠 (jadeite) takes its name from the kingfisher bird — 翡 for the male's red feathers and 翠 for the female's green — because the gem's vivid green color reminded people of the kingfisher's brilliant plumage.

meanings: sth shaped like a tassel (e.g. a leaf etc)

components.note: 纟 (thread, silk) — 缨 names a decorative tassel or cord, such as a hat's chin-strap.
婴 (yīng) gives an exact match for 缨's reading.

example.hanzi: 他主动请缨,要求参加这次危险的任务。
example.pinyin: Tā zhǔdòng qǐngyīng, yāoqiú cānjiā zhè cì wēixiǎn de rènwù.
example.english: He volunteered himself, asking to take part in this dangerous mission.
example.fact: 请缨 (qǐngyīng, 'to request the chin-strap') is a classical idiom for volunteering for a difficult mission, tracing back to a Han-dynasty story of a young envoy who asked for a long rope to bind a troublesome foreign king.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 锹 names a shovel, typically with a metal blade.
秋 (qiū) shares 锹's initial sound but not the full syllable — only a partial resemblance.

example.hanzi: 工人拿起铁锹开始挖土。
example.pinyin: Gōngrén ná qǐ tiěqiāo kāishǐ wā tǔ.
example.english: The worker picked up a shovel and started digging the earth.
example.fact: The shovel is one of the most basic and universal hand tools in human history, with digging implements of this shape found across nearly every agricultural civilization long before iron itself was smelted.

components.note: 山 (mountain) — 嵇 names a mountain in Henan, and became a surname associated with it.
禾 (hé) no longer resembles 嵇's modern reading jī — the sound has drifted apart over time, though it's traditionally treated as the phonetic component.

example.hanzi: 嵇康是魏晋时期著名的思想家和音乐家。
example.pinyin: Jī Kāng shì Wèi-Jìn shíqī zhùmíng de sīxiǎngjiā hé yīnyuèjiā.
example.english: Ji Kang was a famous thinker and musician of the Wei-Jin period.
